properties.description:
* WHAT...Catastrophic flooding caused by excessive rainfall is
expected along the San Juan River between Four Corners and Mexican
Hat. This is an emergency situation!

* WHERE...Western Montezuma County in southwestern Colorado...
Southern San Juan County in southeastern Utah...

* WHEN...Until 100 PM MDT Monday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding along San Juan River is occurring with major
flooding forecast. Low-water crossing are inundated with water and
may not be passable. The river is running fast and high. Do not
attempt to cross.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 830 PM MDT, Major flooding is expected to occur along the San
Juan River from Four Corners to Mexican Hat. The San Juan River
is forecast to crest around midnight tonight at the Four Corners,
reaching Montezuma Creek around 5 am MDT Sunday, cresting between
Bluff and Mexican Hat Sunday afternoon and peaking at Mexican Hat
by 5 pm Sunday evening around 36 feet which will exceed all time
record levels. The San Juan River will rise above flood stage
Sunday morning and continue to rise Sunday afternoon to moderate
flood stage, peaking above major flood stage at Mexican Hat by 5
pm Sunday evening.
- This includes the following streams and drainages...
San Juan River
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...

Aneth.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

climb slowly through Moderate Flood Stage through the weekend.

forecast.

inches of water inside homes along the river and canals. Docks at

* IMPACTS...At 8.5 feet, Overbank flow is occurring from just below
the confluence of the Animas and San Juan Rivers at Farmington, and
continuing downriver through Shiprock. At this water level, the
fast flow can result in river bank erosion but otherwise minor
flood damage.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- There is no current observed data. The river has crested and will
generally continue to fall through Sunday.
- Bankfull stage is 7.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river will fall to near flood stage just after
midnight tonight. It will then rise to 9.2 feet early Sunday
morning. It will then fall below flood stage around mid day
Sunday.
- Flood stage is 8.5 feet.
- The San Juan River at Farmington has crested at an all time
record stage Friday.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/abq.

The next statement will be issued Sunday afternoon at noon MDT.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 24 at 2:46PM MST until October 26 at 12:00AM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues. This
rainfall occurred on Wednesday and Thursday.

* WHERE...The Little Colorado River from Winslow to Leupp.

* WHEN...Until midnight MST Sunday Night /100 AM MDT Monday/.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of the Little Colorado River is occurring.
Deadly flooding over low-water crossings.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 240 PM MST /340 PM MDT/, water levels have crested at Winslow
and are expected to fall this evening. However, downstream
impacts will continue at Navajo Route 71 to Birdsprings through
at least Sunday.
- Flooding is occurring along the Little Colorado River.
- For Little Colorado at Winslow:
At 2:00pm MST /3:00pm MDT/ the stage was 18.34 feet.
Flood Stage is 19.0 feet.
Forecast: The river is cresting now and is forecast to fall
through this evening.
Impacts:
At 17.0 feet: Downstream, the approaches to the bridge over the
river on Navajo Route 71 near Bird Springs will flood, and Leupp
will be within 3 feet of flooding problems. The river will crest
at Navajo Route 71 approximately 18 hours after the river crests
at Winslow. Minor lowland overflow on right bank at Winslow.
At 18.0 feet: Flow above this level for approximately 6 hours or
more may cause erosion to the levee and eventual leakage or
failure.
- Additional information is available at weather.gov/flagstaff.
properties.instruction:
Stay away or be swept away! The banks of creeks and washes are
unstable and unsafe during any flooding event.

Low water crossings will become dangerous in heavy rain. Do not
attempt to cross flooded roads. Find an alternate route.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 24 at 9:06PM MDT until October 25 at 3:30PM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Northwestern Valencia County in central New Mexico...
Northeastern Cibola County in west central New Mexico...

* WHEN...Until 330 PM MDT Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Numerous roads
remain closed due to flooding.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 904 PM MDT, emergency management reported continued flooding
in Cubero and Laguna areas due to earlier thunderstorms. Flooding
is already occurring. Radar estimates 3 to 8 inches of rain have
fallen over the area within the last 3 days.
- Flooding impacts will continue, but no additional rainfall is
expected. Flooding will continue along the Rio San Jose.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Grants, Laguna Pueblo, New Laguna, Cubero, Mesita, San Fidel,
Skyline-Ganipa, McCartys, Paraje and Seama.
- http://www.weather.gov/abq/EmergencyPrepFlood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Stay away or be swept away. River banks and culverts can become
unstable and unsafe.
